clue.text: Settlement: yours initially

parts.note: the punctuation mark itself is read as its name, a colon

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word yours

explanation.surface: A settlement offer is put to someone, the deal being theirs to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after 'Settlement' looks like mere punctuation, but it supplies COLON; 'initially' gives Y from 'yours'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a settlement founded by people from another country.

clue.text: Use them in composition, so it's notepaper

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: Advice to use these sheets for composing, since this is notepaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notepaper' is a joke: paper printed with musical notes. 'it's' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed music is paper carrying musical notes, a witty reading of notepaper.

clue.text: Having taken drugs, swimmer's assistant is in a state for the sporting climax

indicators.note: is in places the two pieces inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: Cal is a short form of California, an American state
up is slang for high, as someone is after taking drugs
a fin, or a diver's flipper, helps a swimmer through water

explanation.surface: A doped-up swimming coach is in a frenzy before a big final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' sounds like being agitated, but the state is CAL (California), holding UP and FIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup final is the deciding match of a knockout competition, the high point of the sporting season.

clue.text: Bird taken out to lunch?

definitions.meaning: a common European bird known for its two-note call and laying eggs in other nests
out to lunch is slang for crazy, so someone taken that way has gone mad

explanation.surface: A girlfriend being treated to a midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the bird and, informally, means crazy, just as out to lunch does.

clue.text: 7 Paul Jones' partner into scam

indicators.note: into puts the setter and the partner inside the word for a scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
Paul is the setter, so from his point of view he is me
Dow is Jones's partner in the Dow Jones stock index

explanation.surface: The setter's financial dealings with Jones turn into a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is DROP, the definition. 'Paul' is the puzzle's setter, giving ME; DOW is from the Dow Jones index.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a fall in status or fortune, so a drop.

clue.text: Liberal Democrat money goes to the right first

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, so money
1st, written with the numeral read as I, is the short form of first

explanation.surface: A politician of the centre party puts cash before principle, leaning right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST, the numeral 1 read as the letter I. A Liberal Democrat belongs to Britain's middle-ground party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Democrats sit between Labour and the Conservatives, so a member is an example of a centre politician.

clue.text: Put up with what may be hard or cold

definitions.meaning: to bear or take on a burden

definitions.text: what may be hard or cold
definitions.meaning: a hard one is the motorway verge, and a cold one is a snub

explanation.surface: Tolerating something harsh or chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to bear it; hard shoulder and cold shoulder are set phrases.

clue.text: A taste of relegation

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount of liquid, as in a sip of wine
being sent down to a lower league or rank

explanation.surface: A football team getting a first experience of going down a division.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a small amount of drink, and also a fall, such as a team going down a league.

clue.text: Give a rocket speed

definitions.meaning: British slang for giving someone a severe telling-off
the pace at which something happens

explanation.surface: Propelling a rocket to high velocity.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old verb for scolding them; a rate is also a pace.

clue.text: Little time this time, a waste of time if caught?

definitions.text: a waste of time if caught?

parts.note: min is short for minute, a little time
now is this present time

explanation.surface: A muddle about time, ending with fishing being pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an angler who lands only a tiny fish has wasted the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a very small fish, hardly worth an angler's while to land.

clue.text: Black person's style in broadcast by waves?

indicators.note: in places the hairstyle inside the word for broadcast

parts.note: sent, as a signal is sent out by a transmitter
an Afro is a rounded hairstyle associated with Black people

explanation.surface: A hairstyle is shown on a television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a description of a TV programme; it is SENT, holding AFRO.
explanation.definitionFit: The promenade of a resort lies next to the sea, beside the breaking waves.

clue.text: Albert Steptoe — might I be told I'm randy?

indicators.note: asks what the following words might be turned into, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A character wonders aloud whether he will be called lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Steptoe, the father in the British sitcom Steptoe and Son, was famously called this by his son Harold.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold's catchphrase insult for his lecherous, grubby father Albert in the sitcom.

clue.text: Wherein litmus may be a choice between red and blue?

parts.note: Labour, the red party in British politics, is shortened to Lab
or offers a choice between alternatives
a Tory is a Conservative, whose party colour is blue

explanation.surface: Testing whether litmus paper turns red or blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Litmus turns red for acid and blue for alkali, but here red is Labour and blue Conservative (Tory), the two main British parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper is used for chemical tests, which are carried out in a science workroom.

clue.text: Swab soiled by somebody's surgeon

indicators.note: soiled means made dirty and messed up, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: one's is a way of saying somebody's

explanation.surface: A medical swab is dirtied by someone in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swab' and 'surgeon' set a hospital scene; sawbones is old slang from the days of amputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawbones is an old slang term for a surgeon, from the days of amputations.

clue.text: Dance with goddess around a bar

indicators.note: around puts the goddess outside the other pieces

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A goddess dancing around a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The habanera is a Cuban dance in slow duple time, famous from Carmen.

clue.text: Women bath us in a lather where clothes should be done

indicators.note: in a lather means agitated, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Women bathing in soapy water where laundry ought to be washed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a lather' rearranges BATH US into ASHTUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub for washing laundry is the place where clothes are cleaned.

clue.text: Leaves from here with trains on time

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: Departures leave from this station with trains running on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' suggests departing, but means tea leaves, which come packed in this box.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large box in which tea leaves are shipped.

clue.text: Concubine offering fruit

definitions.meaning: a wife or mistress of a sultan

explanation.surface: A mistress presenting fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a sultan's wife or concubine and also a dried grape.

clue.text: As if by magic, bounder finds something to unfasten either side of him

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear one might unfasten
a cad is a dishonourable man
a bra again, on the other side

explanation.surface: A rogue magically finds a garment to undo on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of him' places A BRA before and after CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Magicians say this word as an incantation when performing a trick, so it accompanies magic.

clue.text: Social security in social security (social security in social security)

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment benefit
UB stands for unemployment benefit, as on the British UB40 card

explanation.surface: Benefits within benefits, repeated in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed part repeats the wordplay, so it is a copy of it, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bracket repeats the first phrase exactly, making it a duplicate or copy.

clue.text: Ill defined? Ill-defined a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: vague means unclear or ill-defined

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is vague and going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill defined?' reads cryptically: a definition of an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is a feverish illness with shivering, so an ill, defined.

clue.text: Temporary settlement affected

definitions.meaning: a group of tents or huts set up for a while

explanation.surface: A temporary site was influenced.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a temporary site of tents; camp also means exaggerated and theatrical.

clue.text: Fruit containing smashed mineral

indicators.note: containing has the fruit hold the other piece

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
smashed means hit hard

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit with a crushed rock inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite is a soft black form of carbon occurring naturally, used in pencil leads.

clue.text: Horse, non-starter, eating cold fruit

indicators.note: eating has the shortened word take the letter inside
non-starter means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: equine means of horses
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A racehorse that failed to start is eating chilled fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' turns EQUINE into QUINE, which takes in C.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit used in jellies.

clue.text: Application of light, result of flashing?

definitions.meaning: the light let in on film or a sensor in photography
what follows indecent showing of the body, or using a camera flash

explanation.surface: Photography terms for light and camera flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is light hitting film, and also indecent showing of oneself in public.

clue.text: Fluid — a sample endlessly being circulated

indicators.note: being circulated means passed around and mixed, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly removes the last letter of the word sample

explanation.surface: A specimen of liquid is passed round the laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts SAMPLE to SAMPL; with A, 'being circulated' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the clear liquid part of blood in which cells are suspended.
